a.d: Intuitive, subjective speculation without specific concrete sensory evidence.
ex: 내일은 날씨가 **맑을 것 같아요**. — I think tomorrow's weather will probably be clear.

b.d: Conjecture based directly on an observed visual or auditory sign in the immediate environment.
ex: 불이 켜진 걸 보니 집에 **있나 봐요**. — Seeing the light on, they must be home.

im-03-01-01.tip: If you have no visual clues, use -(으)ㄹ 것 같다; if you see evidence right now, use -나/은가 보다; if responding with empathy to someone's story, use -겠군요.

answers: 내일 비가 올 것 같아요.
내일 비가 올 것 같아요
im-03-01-01.hint: When making an intuitive prediction about future weather without seeing clouds, use -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요.
im-03-01-01.why: -나 봐요 requires visible real-time evidence. A general guess about tomorrow uses -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요: 비가 올 것 같아요.

items: I can adjust conjecture strength among -(으)ㄹ 것 같다, -나/은가 보다, and -겠군요.
I can state visual and auditory clues that justify my observations.

a.d: Action verbs, as well as 있다 and 없다, take -나 보다 (먹나 봐요, 가나 봐요, 없나 봐요).
ex: 옆집에서 고기를 **굽나 봐요**. — Smelling it, they must be grilling meat next door.

b.d: Descriptive adjectives take -(으)ㄴ가 보다 (바쁜가 봐요, 추운가 봐요, 작은가 봐요).
ex: 선생님이 요즘 많이 **바쁘신가 봐요**. — The teacher seems to be very busy lately.

im-03-01-02.tip: Remember: Verbs = -나 보다. Adjectives = -(으)ㄴ가 보다. 있다/없다 always take -나 보다 (맛있나 봐요, 없나 봐요).

im-03-01-02.q: Fix the verb conjugation attached to an adjective with -나 보다.
im-03-01-02.wrong: 오늘 날씨가 밖을 보니 꽤 춥나 봐요.
answers: 오늘 날씨가 밖을 보니 꽤 추운가 봐요.
오늘 날씨가 밖을 보니 꽤 추운가 봐요
im-03-01-02.hint: 춥다 is an adjective (ㅂ-irregular). It must take -(으)ㄴ가 보다: 추운가 봐요.
im-03-01-02.why: Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ가 보다. 춥다 conjugates irregularly as 추운가 봐요 (never 춥나 봐요).

ko: 동네 골목에 새로 생긴 베이커리 앞에 아침 일찍부터 손님들이 길게 줄을 서 있었어요.

en: In front of a newly opened bakery in the neighborhood alley, customers were lined up long from early morning.

A huge discount billboard
A TV broadcast truck parked outside

a.d: Deduction derived from immediate observation; tone is wondering, speculative, or thinking aloud.
ex: 저기 사람들이 모인 걸 보니 **무슨 일이 생겼나 봐요**. — Seeing people gathered there, something must have happened.

b.d: Deduction reacting to what someone just shared; tone is warm, understanding, and validating their hardship or joy.

im-03-01-03.tip: Use -나 보다 when you are the observer looking around. Use -겠군요 as a conversational response validating someone's experience.

items: I can use -겠군요 to express heartfelt empathy when listening to others' stories.

a.d: Essential tool in Korean business etiquette to acknowledge hard work, client fatigue, or milestone accomplishments.
ex: 먼 길 오시느라 **고생 많으셨겠군요**. — Having traveled such a long distance, you must have gone through a lot of trouble.

b.d: Used gently to make non-confrontational deductions about schedules or missing colleagues.
ex: 회의가 아직 **안 끝났나 봐요**. — Seeing the door shut, the meeting must not be over yet.

im-03-01-04.tip: In corporate Korean, -겠군요 builds rapport with clients and coworkers, while -나 봐요 softens tentative remarks.
